message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average) | Dominated by protium (¹H). |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium, 99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, 0.02 %), ³H (tritium, trace, radioactive). | Deuterium used in heavy‑water reactors; tritium in nuclear fusion research. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Highest of all elements. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) | Negative, meaning H⁻ formation is endothermic. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; hydrogen is a gas at room temperature. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solidifies only at cryogenic temperatures. |
| **Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | Very light; lighter than air. |
| **Molar volume (ideal gas)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | Standard at 0 °C, 1 atm. |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | Strong covalent bond in H₂. |
| **Dipole moment** | 0 D (homonuclear diatomic) | Non‑polar molecule. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides (H⁻) with metals, acids (H⁺), and many nonmetals. | Forms covalent bonds with electronegative atoms; can form ionic bonds in metal hydrides. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series (UV, visible, IR) | Classic hydrogen emission spectrum. |
| **Phase at STP** | Gas | Exists as H₂ diatomic molecules. |
| **Molecular weight** | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ (H₂) | Twice the atomic mass. |
| **Solubility in water** | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 20 °C | Low; hydrogen is poorly soluble. |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % in air | Requires careful handling. |
| **Applications** | Fuel cells, rocket propellant, hydrogenation reactions, metallurgy, semiconductor manufacturing, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents). | Also used in spectroscopy and fundamental physics experiments. |

### Quick Takeaways

- **Atomic simplicity**: One proton, one electron → the simplest element.
- **High electronegativity & ionization energy**: Makes it a strong oxidizing agent.
- **Low boiling/melting points**: Exists as a gas under normal conditions.
- **Strong H–H bond**: Requires significant energy to break.
- **Versatile chemistry**: Forms hydrides, acids, and fuels; key in energy technologies.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
